answer_plain: If cloud seeding really added ten percent more rain on rainy days, hydrogen uptake over two weeks would rise by about 13 % (by 3.6 to 31 %), so under that rain boost uptake goes up in every case we tried. Whether seeding adds that much rain at all is disputed. When extra water does fall on wet days, it pushes moisture deeper into the sand and keeps microbes active for longer after the rain.
answer_science: Central percentage change: h2_uptake_change_pct = 12.69 % (median 12.83 %, 50 % IQR [8.198, 18.81] %, joint 5–95 % interval [3.596, 31.16] %) (rounded headline: 13 %); absolute change h2_uptake_contrast_umol_m2 = 139.9 µmol m⁻² (median 111.9 µmol m⁻², 50 % IQR [46.42, 249.4] µmol m⁻², joint 5–95 % interval [16.12, 500.3] µmol m⁻²); absolute uptake h2_uptake_umol_m2 = 1242 µmol m⁻² (median 1086 µmol m⁻², 50 % IQR [389.5, 2502] µmol m⁻², joint 5–95 % interval [152.2, 5248] µmol m⁻²) (mode = variance, refusal fraction = 0.0 %, max level refusal across question = 0.0 %). Top two Sobol' contributors to output variance: cloud_seeding_rain_increase_frac (ST = 0.43 [0.37, 0.50], S1 = 0.33) and retention_b (ST = 0.29 [0.24, 0.34], S1 = 0.19). Status share of variance: verified_in_source ST = 0.00 (S1 = 0.00), modeller_assumption ST = 0.98 (S1 = 1.02), source_not_checked ST = 0.00 (S1 = 0.00) (joint group total indices can sum to more than 1 because of interactions). Limits: The parameter-uncertainty interval quantifies joint variation over literature constants and twin process parameters only and excludes external-model and twin model-structure error.

limits_plain: The range shows how much the answer moves when uncertain numbers in the models are varied; the models themselves could also be wrong. Cloud seeding can only add water when suitable clouds are already present; the twin does not predict when clouds form.
limits_science: The parameter-uncertainty interval quantifies joint variation over literature constants and twin process parameters only and excludes external-model and twin model-structure error. Treats seeding as a multiplicative scaling on existing rain-day precipitation; atmospheric microphysics and cloud availability are external to the soil twin.

admissibility.scope: Joint parameter and literature-constant uncertainty only; excludes model-structure error.
